data.title: Senate adopts resolution honoring Fiona the hippo
data.description:
The U.S. Senate adopted a resolution Friday to honor Fiona the hippo, a beloved inhabitant of the Cincinnati Zoo who died Thursday.

Fiona the hippo died days after she ingested a zoo-goers’ hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure. Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) spoke from the floor to mourn the loss of Fiona.

“Fiona was a symbol of resilience, of perseverance and we are going to miss her in Cincinnati,” Moreno said, standing next to a picture of the hippo. 

The zoo announced Thursday that Fiona’s ingestion of the hat eventually turned into a medical emergency. They said the vet team performed supportive care in an attempt to save the hippo but was ultimately unsuccessful. 

“The people who come to our city, our state, that now don’t have Fiona there,” Moreno said. “It’s going to leave a hole in the zoo and a hole in their heart.”

The senator said what happened was a tragic accident and a “devastating loss” to the whole zoo. Moreno noted he offered the resolution to honor the hippo and the greater Cincinnati Zoo team, and the resolution passed through the chamber by unanimous consent. 

“Fiona was nothing but a ray of sunshine,” Moreno said.

data.title: DeSantis calls Supreme Court justices 'potted plants'
data.description:
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) shut down claims in an interview published Friday that he’s interested in a seat on the Supreme Court — an assertion coming as buzz surrounding his plans for 2028 mounts.

DeSantis sat for an extended conversation with The New York Times earlier this week, speaking with the outlet about his future political ambitions. When asked about the prospect about sitting on the high court, the outgoing governor, who ran for president in 2024, described himself as an “executive” by nature and said he would not enjoy the lifestyle of a justice. 

“To say that you’re going to end up a potted plant on the Supreme Court and just kind of sit there,” DeSantis told the Times. 

He added, “And I respect the justices, and people like Clarence Thomas have been heroes of mine for many years, but it just — it’s totally contrary to what I’ve demonstrated and brought to the table.”

The governor has an extensive legal background. A Harvard Law School graduate and Navy veteran, DeSantis served as a military lawyer at Guantanamo Bay before being deployed to Iraq in the 2000s.

Axios reported in April that DeSantis was jockeying for a position in the Trump administration after his term ends in January, allegedly weighing bids for U.S. attorney general or for a position on the Supreme Court.

In the Times interview, DeSantis questioned whether the 2028 presidential election will be a winning cycle for his party and left open the possibility of launching another campaign for the White House.

Nevertheless, he took a swing at Vice President Vance, whom many regard as one of DeSantis’s likely opponents for the presidency, saying he believes President Trump’s second-in-command will struggle to win over the current administration’s detractors.

data.title: House Democrats reup support for McIver after appeals court denies petition
data.description:
House Democrats rallied behind Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-N.J.) on Friday, after a federal appeals court declined her petition for a full panel to consider dismissing charges tied to a scuffle outside of an immigration detention facility in her state earlier this year. 

McIver, who argued her visit to Delaney Hall detention facility was carried out in her official capacity as a member of Congress and should be shielded from prosecution, now faces trial on three federal charges. 

The New Jersey Democrat called the decision from the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals “frustrating” in a statement shared on social platform X.

“Donald Trump continues to send warning shots to Democrats in Congress and in all levels of power but their case against me right now, in broad daylight, goes well beyond a warning,” she wrote. 

Other Democratic allies came to her defense, including Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), the ranking member on the House Judiciary Committee. 

“President Trump’s obsession with jailing my colleague @RepLaMonica for doing her job is wholly antithetical to the Constitution and absurd given the orgy of corruption and criminality taking place in his office and administration,” Raskin wrote online. 

“Members of Congress have a right to conduct oversight of ICE and Border Patrol free from intimidation and prosecution,” he added.

Democratic Rep. Analilia Mejia (N.J.) also responded to McIver’s statement in solidarity with her fellow New Jersey lawmaker.

“Congressional oversight is not a crime; it is our job,” Mejia wrote in a social media post. “No member of Congress should face threats from our President for protecting her constituents. We are fighting for justice and accountability for the American people, and we will not back down.”

In August, a three-judge panel refused to throw out the case, finding that her efforts to prevent the arrest of Newark Mayor Ras Baraka (D) was not protected under the speech and debate clause. 

On Friday, Colorado Rep. Jason Crow (D) accused Trump of attempting to jail the lawmaker “because she’s not afraid to hold this President accountable for his failures.”

“He is weaponizing the Justice Department against those of us who dare stand up to him—but we will not cow to his threats or abuses of power,” Crow wrote on X. 

McIver clashed with Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin during a House hearing earlier this week, telling the secretary that DHS was “killing people.”

When he denied this accusation, she doubled down. 

“You are killing people,” she continued. “The whole entire country watches you kill people, literally.”

data.title: New report highlights mental health struggles of NHL goalies
data.description:
(NewsNation) — A new report highlighting the mental health struggles faced by goalies in the National Hockey League (NHL) found nearly a third of all players publicly known to have sought support from the NHL Players’ Association assistance program were goalies.

Former NHL goalie Corey Hirsch told NewsNation it’s a very real concern among players and that mental illness doesn’t discriminate.

“The thing about mental health is it doesn’t discriminate. It doesn’t care if you’re a broadcaster, a doctor, a lawyer. It doesn’t care if you have a hundred million dollars in your bank account or if you have $5 in your bank account,” he said.

Hirsch, a former goalie with the New York Rangers, Vancouver Canucks, Washington Capitals and Dallas Stars, added that he too has struggled with mental health issues in the past.

“But the problem is reaching out for help, right?” he continued. “That’s the mentality; it’s so cutthroat in professional sports that there’s a guy waiting right behind you to take your job. So that’s probably the main issue is reaching out for help, but it seems to be more prevalent with goaltending.”

The Athletic’s report highlights goalies are frequently the brunt of online harassment, including death threats to themselves and their families.

“The goalie is the last line of defense. So, they’re going to blame them … but the death threats and stuff? I mean, that has to stop,” Hirsch told NewsNation.

He added, “Why would you even do that? Like, why would a person do that to another human being?”

data.title: Vance deflects on whether Iran war worth political price
data.description:
Vice President Vance dodged the question on Friday of whether he thought the Iran war was worth Republicans losing big in the midterm elections earlier this month.

“The president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again,” Vance said at the press briefing alongside President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

“What I’ve said is the goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we should be doing,” he said. “It’s the biggest state sponsor of terrorism. If they had a nuclear weapon, they would use it as leverage, or God forbid, they would attack and kill 1000s, hundreds of 1000s, potentially of innocent people.”

When pressed on whether he thinks it was worth it, Vance said: “My view is that my goal is, and my job is to support the president of the United States. 

Vance, in a lengthy post to the social platform X after the midterms, blamed the ongoing Iran war for Republicans losing the House and the Senate to Democrats.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance said on social media.

“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest,” he continued. “But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.” 

Trump said on Friday that he had “no problem” with Vance’s social media post, adding that it was “very accurate,” but said that he would’ve added that he still would have started the Iran war all over again despite the losses.

“I thought the statement was fine, except I would have had one other thing, that I would have said that – ‘Would you do it again?’ And absolutely, the answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon,” he said.

data.title: Watch live: Trump, Dana White host helipad reception honoring Marine Band
data.description:
President Trump and UFC CEO Dana White will host a reception Friday honoring the United States Marine Band on the White House’s newly renovated helipad.

The president and White are expected to announce a combined $200,000 personal donation to the band, which also performed at the UFC 250 fight over the summer. Taxpayer dollars will not fund the contribution, according to the Trump administration.

“The President’s Own’ United States Marine Band proudly embodies American excellence and tradition — and their melodies have accompanied defining moments in our nation’s history,” White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said in a statement.

“President Trump will partner with Dana White to generously celebrate their elite musical talent and unwavering dedication, conveying his gratitude to some of our Nation’s finest musicians,” she added.

The event marks the first official gathering at the new White House installation, part of Trump’s ongoing upgrades to the campus. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao are also expected to attend.

The reception is scheduled to begin at 3:30 p.m. EST.

Watch live above.

data.title: Trump opens door to deals with Democrats on healthcare, Hollywood, college sports
data.description:
President Trump left the door open to working with Democrats on issues like health care, Hollywood, and college sports regulations during his news conference on Friday. 

“I am open to great health care. Now, can it be what they want? No, but it can be a combination of what we all want. We could end up with great health care in our country. We could end up better than dealing with just the Republicans. We’ll have tremendous Republican support,” Trump told reporters. 

The president went on to discuss how the administration was working with Congress to incentivize filming more movies and television shows in the U.S., citing the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. 

“It has unbelievable support. I’ll tell you what, [Sen.] Adam Schiff said ‘wow, we love that bill,’” Trump said of the California Democrat.  

“That’s going to be very bipartisan, and I can tell you it’s going to happen,” he continued. 

Trump also said he saw opportunities to work with Democrats on legislation that would establish national standards for NIL [name, image, and likeness] in college sports.” 

“So, you’re going to have colleges, every college is going to go bankrupt if we don’t get a bill done because they’re going crazy. They’re paying quarterbacks $12 million a year,” the president told reporters, warning colleges are going to go “bankrupt.” 

Trump said he has been in touch with Democrats on Capitol Hill following their sweeping midterm election wins earlier this month, though he didn’t name individual lawmakers.

Trump previously said that he would be open to working with Democrats on immigration reform, but his move to name Stephen Miller as his chief of staff was seen by many Democrats as a sign that compromise is unlikely.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.)  was overwhelmingly elected to be speaker in the new Congress earlier this week, while Senate Minority Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) is in a leadership race against progressive Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.). 

Trump said both Jeffries and Schumer were “smart” and would eventually work with him after enough vetoes.

“You know, there are those that say we might get more done because we had some Republicans that were just impossible to deal with,” he said.

data.title: Consistent bedtimes could protect your heart health, new study
data.description:
(NewsNation) — The consistency of your sleep schedule may be more important than the number of hours slept in preventing adverse heart events, according to a new study.

The research, published in Circulation: Population Health and Outcomes, looked at over 10,000 participants who wore a Fitbit over the course of six months. Researchers broke down sleep data by quality, quantity, regularity, timing and number of sleep cycles.

Night-to-night changes in sleep timing were linked to a 20-23 percent increased risk of a serious heart event. These risks included heart failure, acute myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy and ischemic strokes.

Each 29-minute increase in sleep length from night to night increased the likelihood of a serious heart event by 24 percent. Specifically, researchers observed a 20 percent increased risk of heart failure and a 29 percent increased risk of cardiomyopathy.

Surprisingly, sleep duration was not associated with any major heart-related risks.

These findings challenge the age-old notion that the most important factor in healthy sleep is how many hours you get.

“Our finding is surprising because we can see the dominance of regularity instead of quantity,” lead researcher Nguyen Minh Tuan Viet, MD, PhD said in a press release. “Adequate quantity of sleep had some protective effect, but lack of sleep did not have much harmful effect in the study.”

The study did not establish cause and effect, but they point out a key controllable aspect of sleep that people can use to protect their health. However, more research is needed to establish if intervention lowers the risk of heart-related issues.

“Sometimes we can’t control the total amount of sleep, but the regularity- that is the thing that we can actively control,” Nguyen said. “But the regularity- consistent bedtimes throughout the week and waking up at the same time every morning, is something some people can control.”

data.title: Justice Department taps new attorney to lead controversial review of Trump probes
data.description:
The Justice Department (DOJ) has tapped Bill Essayli, an embattled federal prosecutor in California, to additionally take on a sprawling Florida-based probe into the past investigations of President Trump.

Essayli was found last month to be unlawfully serving in his post as First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California beyond the 120 days allowed for vacancies.

But the DOJ confirmed Essayli will now take on additional duties in the Southern District of Florida, which has housed a probe looking into the 2022 search of Mar-a-Lago as well as other matters involving the president.

He’ll be stepping into a role that has resulted in numerous prosecutors leaving the department.

Trump ally Joe diGenova, who had stepped in to lead the probe, resigned in September over apparent concerns about the speed of the investigation. 

In an interview that month with the New York Post, diGenova suggested there were larger issues with the investigation.

“If you want indictments where there’s no evidence, you have an ethical problem,” he told the outlet.

Maria Medetis Long, a career DOJ official who also played a leading role in the case, resigned in April, reportedly over concerns about the strength of the case.

Jason Reding Quinones, who had been serving as the U.S. attorney for the district, resigned shortly after the midterms.

Essayli has overseen the DOJ’s legal fight with California officials over 20,000 noncitizens allegedly on state voter rolls. The prosecutor said thedepartment’s request to California counties to identify potential noncitizens on their voter rolls was “simple” and said election officials not complying with the DOJ will be held accountable.

data.title: Live updates: Trump, Vance and Rubio brief reporters on China summit; GOP at odds over reconciliation
data.description:
President Trump, fresh from his trip to Asia, is briefing reporters on his trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are also joining the president for Friday’s briefing.

Trump touted the rare summit as “Great and Highly Consequential” in a post online following the meeting. Earlier Thursday, the trio announced the talks yielded a symbolic “declaration toward peace.”

Meanwhile, Senate Republicans are increasingly at odds over the Trump administration’s push for a $350 billion Pentagon funding package. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) warned that the reconciliation process could expose deep divisions within the GOP over Medicaid cuts enacted last year.

Some lawmakers are eager to revisit the healthcare reductions, while others fear reopening the debate could unravel key provisions of Trump’s signature tax law. Hill Insiders can learn more here.

On Thursday, Senate Republicans blocked another war powers resolution that would restrict further military operations in Iran. The upper chamber did advance the bipartisan permitting reform bill though, sending it to the House.

A federal district court in Virginia will also hear arguments Friday on a lawsuit seeking to prevent the construction of Trump’s proposed 250-foot triumphal arch. The hearing comes two days after a federal judge extended the block on construction.

Trump will host a reception in the afternoon and hold signing time. First lady Melania Trump, whose docuseries premiered late Thursday on Prime Video, will attend an arrival ceremony for the White House Christmas tree.

Follow live below.
